style.name: The Verdigris Sanctuary of Qamar-Ashan (Mughal red-sandstone and verdigris)
style.rationale: Second pass: the minarets are now engaged. Each is bonded to the main block by a two-tier niched flanking bay, so no sky shows between the tower and the body at the base. The 11-wide pishtaq projects 2 blocks ahead of the wings. Its gold calligraphy frame wraps verdigris spandrels, and its 7-wide pointed iwan has a stepped chiseled inner jamb before a dark-prismarine back. That back carries a copper lattice window and a recessed copper doorway with a gold head. The wings are split into integrated bays by projecting pilasters that rise into gold-tipped pinnacles. Each wing has two tiers of 2-deep pointed niches with copper spandrels and lattice windows, plus string courses, a cornice, a copper frieze and a merlon parapet, so no field is left flat. The chamfered corners carry dark inset panels. The plinth is a full blind arcade with dark-prismarine recesses and a copper arch-head band, and a central stair leads up to it. The crown is tightened into one stepped pyramid: an engaged guldasta shaft on each side of the pishtaq, a gold-banded drum, a 19-wide onion dome modeled in curving relief, two copper-domed chhatris with dark interiors, and minaret chhatris with gold finials. The coral cut red sandstone stays dominant against verdigris copper, with dark-prismarine shadow and sparing gold accents, so the facade holds its colour instead of drifting toward the reference's white.
